status: FROZEN before any site report was read. One reachability test (a DoA archive search for 'Machaerus', titles only) was made before this file was written.
purpose: Exploratory. Build a gazetteer of Second Temple-period sites east of the Jordan with Jewish, Hasmonean or Herodian occupation, and a table of their recorded features, so that the joint model can replace its single 'transjordan' proxy (Goranson's Transjordan reading of Kohlit) with documented places. No identification claim.

area.name: Peraea and the east bank of the Jordan valley and Dead Sea, Yarmuk to Arnon
area.south_limit: Wadi Mujib (Arnon) mouth, about 31.46 N; sites south of the Arnon are out
area.north_limit: Yarmuk river, about 32.64-32.70 N; sites north of the Yarmuk are out
area.west_limit: the Jordan river and the east shore of the Dead Sea (sites must lie east of the line)
area.east_limit_rule: great-circle distance from the site point to the nearest point of the river/shore polyline below, computed in a local equirectangular projection; sites more than 40.0 km away are out
area.polyline_basis: INFERENCE: approximate points along the Jordan (Yarmuk confluence, Sheikh Hussein bridge, Damiya, King Hussein bridge, Jordan mouth) and the Dead Sea east shore (Zara, Mujib mouth), from general maps; precision about 1-2 km, enough for a 40 km cut-off
area.josephus_peraea_flag: peraea_proper = yes if the site lies inside Josephus's Peraea (War 3.46-47: length from Machaerus to Pella, breadth from Philadelphia to the Jordan), i.e. between the latitudes of Machaerus and Pella and west of Philadelphia (Amman), and is not a Decapolis city (Pella, Gadara, Gerasa, Philadelphia, Abila of the Decapolis). Recorded as INFERENCE.

period.mapping_column: dated_in_window, with values yes / overlaps / no / undated

mapping_rules.yes: the source dates the feature or occupation wholly inside the window: Hasmonean, Herodian, Early Roman, Late Hellenistic (2nd-1st c. BCE), 1st c. BCE, 1st c. CE, early 2nd c. CE, or explicit years inside 152 BCE - 135 CE
mapping_rules.overlaps: the source gives a period that straddles the window: 'Hellenistic' undivided, 'Roman' undivided, 'Hellenistic-Roman', 'Classical', 'Nabataean' without a sub-date
mapping_rules.no: the source dates it wholly outside the window (Iron Age, Persian, Early Hellenistic before 152 BCE, Late Roman after 135 CE, Byzantine, Islamic)
mapping_rules.undated: the source gives no date for the feature

period.rule: A feature counts as dated in window only if the source itself dates it so (yes). 'overlaps' is reported separately and never counted as yes. The period is recorded as the source gives it in period_as_given.

jewish_hasmonean_herodian_markers.textual: Josephus, 1-2 Maccabees or rabbinic texts name the site as Jewish, Peraean, held or built by a Hasmonean ruler, or held or built by Herod or Herod Antipas
jewish_hasmonean_herodian_markers.archaeological: the excavator reports Hasmonean or Herodian construction, Jewish ritual baths (miqvaot), chalk/stone vessels, Hasmonean coins as a period marker, or Jewish (Hebrew/Aramaic) inscriptions, inside the window

inclusion_rules.site_in_gazetteer: The site is in the area AND has at least one of the markers above. Every site seeded below is searched and recorded, including those that fail, with the reason.
inclusion_rules.status_documented: occupation inside the window (dated_in_window = yes) is EVIDENCE from an archaeological report, AND a Jewish/Hasmonean/Herodian marker is EVIDENCE (textual statement or archaeological report)
inclusion_rules.status_partial: one of the two is only INFERENCE or TRADITION (for example, the ancient name's identification with the modern site is disputed, or occupation is only 'Roman' undivided)
inclusion_rules.status_excluded: outside the area, or no marker, or no occupation in or overlapping the window
inclusion_rules.evidence_labels: Each criterion is labelled EVIDENCE (a source states it), INFERENCE (our reasoning), TRADITION (later tradition, for example Byzantine pilgrim identification) or CLAIM (a modern proposal not yet tested)
inclusion_rules.feature_row: one row per feature per source. A feature belongs to a site if the source places it in the site or within 2 km of the site's centre point. Quotes are 12 words or fewer.
inclusion_rules.decapolis_cities: Pella, Gadara (Umm Qais), Gerasa and Philadelphia are recorded with the textual marker only if Josephus says a Hasmonean ruler held or took them; they get peraea_proper = no.

order_of_sources: a coordinate or grid reference printed in an excavation report
Wikidata coordinate (as the W2B model already does)
INFERENCE from a published map, labelled
coordinates.sigma_km_rule: sigma = the larger of (a) the source point's precision (Pleiades accuracy value if given; 0.1 km for a printed grid reference to 100 m), (b) half the site's stated extent, and (c) 0.2 km. If the ancient name's location is disputed between named alternatives, the row uses the main identification and sigma at least half the distance to the farthest alternative; the alternatives are listed.

sources_in_order.what: Department of Antiquities of Jordan publication archive (ADAJ, SHAJ, Munjazat, Athar): search page and open PDFs
ACOR 'Archaeology in Jordan' newsletters and other open ACOR reports
Pleiades gazetteer place records (coordinates, ancient names, attestations)
Josephus, War and Antiquities, Whiston translation (public domain), Project Gutenberg
other open excavation reports and articles (open-access journals, institutional repositories)

not_used: MEGA-Jordan and EAMENA (logins required): access route recorded only
any paywalled, lending or shadow library

procedure: 1. For each seed site, search DOA with each search term (title search), list hits, and read the most relevant open reports (excavation reports and surveys first) for the site's period evidence and features.
2. Search ACOR newsletters for the site names.
3. Take coordinates from Pleiades (or the order above) and apply the sigma rule.
4. Check the textual marker in Josephus (Whiston) and cite book.section.
5. Code gazetteer.csv and features.csv; record every failed link and every source not read.
6. Stop rule: about 30 report PDFs in all; prefer first reports and synthesis articles; record what is left unread.
model_link: The model variant's rule is frozen separately in PLAN_v3.md, after the gazetteer is built and before the model is run.
limits: Exploratory. No identification claim. Silence is never absence. Quotes 12 words or fewer; no PDFs or page images in the repository.
